NOTE: The official merit badge pamphlets are now free and downloadable HERE or can be purchased at the Scout Shop.

requirements.lead_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following:
requirements.req_text: Safety and Registration. Do the following: (a) Explain to your counselor the hazards you are most likely to encounter during automotive maintenance activities, and what you should do to anticipate, help prevent, mitigate, or lessen these hazards. (b) Discuss with your counselor the safety equipment, tools, and clothing used while checking or repairing a motor vehicle. Use this equipment, tools, and/or clothing (when needed or called for) in meeting the requirements for this merit badge. (c) Explain the different ways motor vehicles are powered. (d) Explain the safety considerations when performing maintenance on a vehicle equipped with a high-voltage electrical system. (e) Review the maintenance chart in the vehicle owner's manual. Explain the requirements and time limits. (f) Explain the purpose, importance, and limitations of safety belts and passive restraints. (g) Find out the requirements for your state's emissions and safety inspections (as applicable), including how often a vehicle needs to be inspected. (h) Explain the importance of registering a vehicle and find out the annual registration fee for renewing your family car's registration.

pamphlet_excerpts: Hazard Prevention: Secure elevated vehicles on rated jack stands before placing any limb underneath.
Eye Protection: Wear ANSI Z87 approved safety glasses during all fluid checks and mechanical work.
Toxicity Control: Collect hazardous fluids in sealed containers to prevent skin contact and environmental runoff.
Electrical Safety: Disconnect the negative battery terminal before servicing any starting or charging circuit components.
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 - Protective Equipment Setup: Put on ANSI rated safety glasses and chemical resistant nitrile gloves before starting.
Step 2 - Parking Brake Engagement: Shift into park, set the emergency brake, and place chocks behind opposite wheels.
Step 3 - High Voltage Clearance: Check for orange high voltage cables and turn off ignition keys completely.
Step 4 - Documentation Review: Open the vehicle owner manual to locate factory service schedules and registration records.

left_points: (1a) Automotive Shop Hazard Mitigation: Automotive maintenance introduces severe hazards including chemical exposure, mechanical pinch points, hot exhaust components, and heavy falling objects. Technicians anticipate risks by setting wheel chocks, confirming mechanical lockouts, and wearing appropriate protective gear.

(1b) Personal Protective Equipment Standards: Technicians must wear fitted cotton work clothes, steel-toed footwear, and impact-resistant safety glasses while working around rotating machinery. Rings, necklaces, and loose ties present severe entanglement risks around active drive belts and cooling fans.

(1c) Motor Vehicle Powertrain Architectures: Vehicles derive motive power from gasoline internal combustion, diesel compression ignition, hybrid gas-electric drivetrains, or pure battery electric motors. Each powertrain architecture requires distinct maintenance procedures and safety protocols.
right_points: (1e) Manufacturer Maintenance Schedule Interpretation: Owner manuals provide detailed mileage and calendar intervals for replacing vital fluids, friction materials, and air filters. Scouts must interpret both normal and severe operating schedules to preserve engine warranties.

(1f) Passenger Restraint System Dynamics: Three-point lap and shoulder belts secure occupants within the vehicle survival space, while supplemental restraint airbags cushion head impacts. Airbags can cause fatal concussive injuries if passengers fail to wear primary safety belts correctly.

(1g) State Emissions Inspection Mandates: State safety and emissions programs verify that running gear, braking systems, illumination devices, and catalytic emission controls satisfy environmental and public safety statutes. Testing cadence typically follows annual or biennial requirements depending on local municipal regulations.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
quiz_item.question: You are preparing to crawl beneath a vehicle to inspect the exhaust and suspension for Automotive Maintenance Requirement 1. Which safety procedure is strictly required before anyone goes under the car?
options: A. Raise one corner of the bumper with the emergency scissor jack from the trunk, leave the transmission in neutral, and crawl underneath immediately.
B. Keep the engine running inside a closed garage to warm the fluids while supporting the frame on hollow concrete cinder blocks.

C. Park on a firm level surface, set the parking brake, chock the wheels, lift the vehicle at manufacturer-specified jack points, and lower it onto rated mechanical jack stands before going underneath.
D. Stack wooden two-by-fours on top of a hydraulic floor jack saddle and rely on the hydraulic cylinder pressure alone to hold the vehicle up.

Alignment Geometry: Align caster, camber, and toe angles to prevent premature edge wear and pulling.

left_points: (4a) Tire Specification Placard Comparison: Vehicle door jamb placards detail the exact tire dimensions and cold inflation pressures engineered for optimal braking and handling. Sidewall stampings specify only the maximum permissible pressure and load ratings of the tire casing itself.

(4b) Tire Pressure Inflation Protocols: Technicians use calibrated mechanical or digital gauges to assess tire pressures when vehicles have rested for three hours. Compact spare tires operate at significantly higher pressures, typically sixty pounds per square inch, and require routine maintenance.
right_points: (4c) Wheel Alignment Geometry Fundamentals: Suspension alignment encompasses camber, caster, and toe angles which position the tire perpendicular to the road surface during cornering. comparison_data.left_header: Req 8a: Starting and Charging System Compo
left_points: (8a) Starting and Charging System Components: Vehicle electrical architectures integrate a storage battery, starter motor, and belt-driven alternator to manage electrical demands. Lighting and auxiliary systems draw regulated direct current power through fused circuits protected by electronic relays.

(8b) Engine Cylinder Firing Orders: Engine firing orders establish the precise sequence in which individual spark plugs ignite compressed air-fuel charges across cylinders. Distributing power strokes evenly balances rotational forces along the crankshaft, preventing excessive mechanical vibration.

(8c) Spark Plug Gap Calibration: The spark plug gap provides the physical separation across which ignition coils discharge thousands of volts to ignite the air-fuel mixture. Setting the gap to exact manufacturer tolerances ensures reliable flame kernel propagation and prevents engine misfires.
right_points: (8d) Safe Battery Jumper Connections: Jumping a dead vehicle battery requires strict attachment sequences to avoid sparking near explosive hydrogen gas pockets. Clamping positive cables first and ending with an unpainted engine block ground prevents hazardous battery explosions.

(8e) Electric Vehicle Range Factors: Electrified vehicle range depends on battery pack temperature, aggressive acceleration habits, aerodynamic drag, and auxiliary cabin heating loads. Recharging involves connecting dedicated Level 1, Level 2, or direct current fast-charging connectors through standardized charge ports.

(8f) Electrical Subsystem Dependencies: A stable electrical system powers electronic control modules, electric power steering racks, antilock braking solenoids, and safety sensors. Voltage drops trigger sensor calibration faults and induce transmission limp-mode lockouts.

left_points: (9a) Drivetrain Component Architecture: The drivetrain consists of the transmission, driveshafts, universal or constant-velocity joints, differential gears, and drive axles. These components multiply engine torque and transmit rotational power smoothly across flexible suspension geometries.

(9b) Transmission Mechanism Comparison: Manual transmissions require driver-actuated mechanical friction clutches to disengage gears during gear changes. Automatic transmissions utilize torque converters and electronically controlled planetary gearsets to execute smooth gear ratio shifts automatically.
right_points: (9c) Automatic Transmission Fluid Specifications: Automatic transmission fluids feature unique friction modifier formulations, detergent packages, and viscosity characteristics engineered for specific manufacturer transmissions. Utilizing unapproved fluid specifications causes internal wet clutch slippage and overheating.

(9d) Gearbox and Differential Lubricants: Manual transmissions, transfer cases, and differentials require high-viscosity gear lubricants engineered for extreme pressures and hypoid bevel gear shear forces. Hypoid gear lubricants protect differential ring and pinion teeth under heavy towing loads.
